assertions.evidence: Both scalar/quat.rs:184 and sse/quat.rs:170 have 'pub fn inverse(&self) -> Self { self.conjugate() }' — a single-line delegation with no duplicate logic. The conjugate implementations are distinct (scalar negates fields, SSE uses XOR mask) but inverse is correctly unified in both backends.

All Vec types use by-value parameter passing for dot, cross, distance, distance_squared, and angle_between: Vec2 (scalar/vec2.rs) uses dot(self, other: Vec2), cross(self, other: Vec2), distance(self, other: Vec2); Vec3 (scalar/vec3.rs) uses dot(self, b: Vec3), cross(self, b: Vec3), distance(self, other: Vec3), angle_between(self, other: Vec3); Vec4 scalar (scalar/vec4.rs) uses dot(self, other: Vec4); Vec4 SSE (sse/vec4.rs) uses dot(self, other: Vec4). No Vec3 SSE backend exists. Convention is consistent.

All Vec::lerp methods use &self calling convention: Vec2 (scalar/vec2.rs) 'pub fn lerp(&self, other: Vec2, t: f32)', Vec3 (scalar/vec3.rs) 'pub fn lerp(&self, other: Vec3, t: f32)', Vec4 scalar (scalar/vec4.rs) 'pub fn lerp(&self, other: Vec4, t: f32)', Vec4 SSE (sse/vec4.rs) 'pub fn lerp(&self, other: Vec4, t: f32)'. All second parameters are by-value (not by-reference).
Vec3::ONE constant defined at scalar/vec3.rs:20 as 'pub const ONE: Vec3 = Vec3([1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0])'. No SSE Vec3 backend exists, so scalar-only is correct.

Mat4 at mat4.rs:14 derives Copy via '#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]'. The commit also removed .clone() calls on Mat4 in downstream files (frustum.rs, plane.rs, ray.rs, skin.rs, renderer.rs, modelcache.rs) since Copy now handles implicit copying.
Mat2 at mat2.rs:6 derives PartialEq via '#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq)]'. The commit replaced a manual PartialEq impl with the derive macro.
Sphere at sphere.rs:3 derives '#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]', covering all three required traits (Debug, PartialEq, Copy). Previously only Clone was derived.

codeReview.summary: The feature comprehensively standardizes katla_math API conventions across all Vec types and both scalar/SSE backends where applicable. All 7 assertions are satisfied. The implementation correctly updated all downstream call sites (19 files touched) to match the new API conventions. Tests pass (350+ tests), workspace compiles, and clippy reports zero warnings.
